thread.title: Apple Shares Gain after Event Showcase

author: Nina Lee
title: Apple Shares Gain after Event Showcase
text:
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL) showcased its upcoming products at its Keynote Event held at the Steve Jobs Theater on its campus in Cupertino, California on Wednesday. Shares gained 1.52% at the opening bell on Thursday.
Apple showcased its new products, starting from its redesigned Apple Watch Series 4 and its updated HomePod, but all the attention was focused on the three new iPhones.
Apple unveiled three of its newest iPhones: the iPhone XR, iPhone XS and iPhone XS Max. The Company said that the larger screen OLED XS Max model would start at USD 1,100.00, the XS would start at USD 1,000.00, and the LCD screen XR would start at USD 749.00.
The iPhone XS Max is slightly bigger than the XS, which is 5.8-inch, while the XS Max is 6.5-inch. Both of the phones run on the same A12 Bionic chip, as well as the XR, delivering the latest and fastest technology.
The A12 Bionic chip allows Apple to deliver more powerful iPhones than its predecessors. The chip is built with a six-core fusion with two performances cores that are 15% year faster, while the four efficiency cores are up to 50% more efficient, and a four-core GPU that is 50% faster.
Along with the new technology, Apple integrated a new dual SIM card, a new 12MP camera, and a larger storage, allowing for longer battery life and faster charging.
Despite the positive reaction to the new iPhones, Goldman Sachs slashed its earnings forecast for Apple. The firm lowered its fiscal 2019 earnings per share estimates to USD 13.77 from USD 14.53, reiterating a neutral rating. The firm also reaffirmed its USD 240.00 12-month price target, according to CNBC .
“Apple rolled out new iPhones as expected but the new LCD ‘XR’ model was priced lower than we had thought likely. This effectively obsoletes two iPhone 8/8+ SKUs in our opinion and drives us to reduce our ASP [average selling price] and earnings estimates, offset slightly by a higher unit forecast,” analyst Goldman Sachs analyst Rod Hall said in a note to clients Wednesday.
Morgan Stanley analysts said the event largely met their expectations. The firm maintained its fiscal year 2019 unit expectations, but raised its iPhone ASP estimates to USD 793.00, up 6% year over year. The firm maintained an overweight rating.
Other firms such as Bank of America also adjusted its estimates to a price target of USD 256.00 from USD 250.00 on an EPS of USD 14.68 for fiscal year 2019, while maintaining a buy rating. Piper Jaffray raised its estimates driven by the new lineup and Guggenheim Securities raised its price target to USD 245.00 and maintained a buy rating.
